desc: Implement a Miller-Rabin primality test to check if $p = k \cdot N + 1$ is prime.
Implement a function to find all prime factors of $N$ (since $N \le 10^9$, trial division up to $\sqrt{N}$ is fast enough).
Implement modular exponentiation for large numbers.

Implement the main loop: iterate $k$ starting from 1, construct $p$, check primality. If prime, find prime factors of $N$, pick a random base $g$, compute $A = g^{(p-1)/N} \pmod p$, and verify the order condition.
Read $T$ test cases and process each one.
Run the code against the provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
Verify edge cases (e.g., $N$ being a large prime, $N$ being a power of 2).
Ensure the code handles input/output format correctly.
